answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by tying participation to a costly, verifiable commitment such as a bonded stake that slashes on provable misbehavior. A single operator cannot cheaply spawn thousands of identities when each one must lock capital. Reputation then acts as a beacon for honest peers, while reward history serves as an anchor that keeps long-term behavior visible. Rewards for relaying useful work are paid slowly, so a flood of fresh fake agents earns little and nectar-style incentives stop attracting pure farms.
